requirements.statement: When content whose reading direction is horizontal is displayed in a window reduced to 320 CSS px wide, all its information and functionality are available without any horizontal scrolling.

citations.quote: lorsque le contenu dont le sens de lecture est horizontal est affiché dans une fenêtre réduite à une largeur de 320 px, l’ensemble des informations et des fonctionnalités sont-elles disponibles sans aucun défilement horizontal (hors cas particuliers) ?
Lorsqu'il est ici question de pixel, il s'agit du pixel CSS
les contenus peuvent-ils être présentés sans perte d’information ou de fonctionnalité

routes.statement: At a width of 320 CSS px, every piece of information and functionality remains available without horizontal scrolling.

citations.quote: Réduire la fenêtre d’affichage à une largeur de 320 px et vérifier que les informations et les fonctionnalités restent disponibles sans aucun défilement horizontal

exceptions.statement: Content whose layout needs two dimensions to be understood or used is exempt, such as images, graphics or videos, games, presentations such as slideshows, data tables, and interfaces that need a horizontal scrollbar while they are used.

citations.quote: Font exception à ce critère, les contenus dont l'agencement requiert deux dimensions pour être compris ou utilisés comme :
Les images, les graphiques ou les vidéos ;
Les jeux (jeux de plateforme, par exemple) ;
Les interfaces où il est nécessaire d'avoir un ascenseur horizontal lors de la manipulation de l'interface.

exceptions.statement: In browsers on mobile operating systems (Android, iOS), which do not reflow correctly on zoom, the criterion is not applicable.

citations.quote: la majorité des navigateurs sur les systèmes d'exploitation sur mobile (Android, iOS) ne gère pas correctement la redistribution en cas de zoom. Dans ce contexte, le critère sera considéré comme non applicable sur ces environnements.

rationale.text: The test has one requirement: at 320 CSS px wide, all information and functionality of horizontally read content are available without horizontal scrolling. The technical note fixes the pixel as the CSS pixel. The particular cases exempt content whose layout needs two dimensions, with a list introduced by 'comme', so as examples: images, graphics, videos, games, slideshows, data tables, interfaces that need a horizontal scrollbar. They also make the criterion not applicable in mobile browsers. Whether a piece of content needs two dimensions, and whether everything the page offers stays available, is judgment in general. The candidate is none. The custom check, on a target whose layout viewport is exactly 320 CSS px in a desktop context, looks for a letter of ordinary prose, in a block that itself fits the width and under a fixed list of plain structural and phrasing ancestors, that lies outside the viewport. Its fault is evidence only, for two reasons. First, a glyph outside the viewport does not prove that information is unavailable: the requirement is about information and functionality, not about each copy of a text. Codex's counter-example is a static page with a white-space:nowrap presentation duplicate of a line, cut off at 320 px, and the same line shown in full just below it in a wrapping paragraph that fits; the information stays available without scrolling, yet the check's predicate holds. Second, the list of ancestors the check accepts and the styles it excludes only make a two-dimensional layout less likely: they cannot prove that a fragment of prose is not part of a comparison or presentation that needs two dimensions, which is the exception. The link keeps its routes and its partial scope and becomes evidence_only. What would raise the entry: a check that establishes an in-scope loss of access to information or functionality (the cut-off content is not available elsewhere within the width) and rules out the two-dimensional exception, keeping the exact viewport and mobile-environment guards, with the duplicated-line case and an ordinary lost-prose case as fixtures. The check examines a target only when its layout viewport is exactly 320 CSS px wide at zoom 100%, reading the width left to the content, since whether a 320 px window counts its scrollbar is not settled by the text. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: the test applies to content read horizontally, which is nearly every page, but whether some content is designed to scroll in the other direction is not decidable by code with certainty. Needs is empty: the width is a property of the target, set by the sample, not an interaction.
